text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: 1) Scaling to 10K Clicks per Second

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Horizontal scaling at every layer: The click processor service scales horizontally behind a load balancer.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Streams like Kafka/Kinesis scale via sharding, and Flink scales by running parallel jobs — one per shard —

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: handling aggregation independently.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Smart sharding strategy: Shard the stream by AdId so all events for the same ad land in the same shard,

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: enabling parallel and independent processing. For self-managed OLAP databases like ClickHouse, shard by

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: AdvertiserId so all of an advertiser's ads live on one node — speeding up multi-ad dashboard queries.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Managed warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery) handle scaling automatically.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Hot shard problem: A viral ad (e.g., Nike + LeBron) sends massive traffic to a single shard, causing latency

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: spikes and potential data loss. All clicks for that AdId hit the same partition, overwhelming it.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Hot shard fix - partition key suffixing: Append a random suffix to popular AdIds (identified by ad spend or

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: historical volume), turning the key into AdId:0-N. This spreads load across multiple partitions. When Flink

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: writes to OLAP, it strips the suffix and uses the original AdId — since writes are upserts with SUM

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: aggregation, concurrent writes from different partitions combine correctly without data loss.

g.text: 2) Ensuring No Click Data Loss

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Stream-level durability built-in: Kafka and Kinesis are distributed, fault-tolerant, and highly available by

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: default — Kafka replicates across brokers, Kinesis across availability zones. Enabling a retention period (e.g.,

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: 7 days) means even if the stream processor crashes, it can come back up and replay missed events directly

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: from the stream.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Checkpointing — useful but often overkill here: Flink supports checkpointing (periodically saving state to

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: S3) so it can resume after failure. This shines for large aggregation windows (days/weeks), but with our tiny

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: minute-level windows, we'd lose at most a minute of work — easily recoverable by replaying the stream.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Pushing back on unnecessary checkpointing is a strong signal of senior-level judgment in interviews.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Periodic reconciliation for correctness: Low latency and perfect correctness are often at odds. To catch

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: transient errors, bad deploys, or out-of-order events, continuously archive raw clicks to a data lake (S3)

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: using Kafka Connect S3 Sink or Kinesis Data Firehose — no extra load on Flink. Then run a daily Spark batch

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: job to re-aggregate from raw events and compare against the stream processor's output, fixing any

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: discrepancies in the OLAP DB.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Lambda Architecture - best of both worlds: This pattern combines a speed layer (Flink) for low-latency

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: results with a batch layer (Spark) acting as the source of truth for correctness. The batch layer periodically

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: reconciles and corrects any inaccuracies from the speed layer, giving you fast and accurate click data.

g.text: 3) Preventing Click Abuse & Enforcing Idempotency

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Naive approach (userId + adId dedup) is insufficient: Requiring login and deduping on userId + adId works

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: only if all users are authenticated and — more critically — breaks retargeting, where the same user is

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: intentionally shown the same ad multiple times. We actually want one click per user per ad instance

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: (impression), not per ad overall.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Impression ID as idempotency key: The Ad Placement Service generates a unique impression ID every time

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: an ad is rendered (1000 views = 1000 unique IDs). This ID is sent to the browser with the ad and returned

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: with the click event, allowing the system to dedup on impression ID — which correctly handles retargeting.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Dedup must happen before the stream, not in Flink: Since Flink aggregates in windows, a duplicate click

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: straddling a minute boundary would be double-counted. Instead, the Click Processor checks a Redis cache for

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: the impression ID — if present, drop it; if not, write to the stream first, then update the cache (writing

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: first ensures no click loss on cache failure; rare duplicates get cleaned up by reconciliation).

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - HMAC signing prevents forged impression IDs: Without protection, attackers could spam fake unique

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: impression IDs and inflate clicks. Sign the impression ID + adId with an HMAC secret key before sending to

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: the browser, then verify on click. HMAC is microsecond-fast (no asymmetric crypto) and also prevents

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: replaying valid IDs against different ads.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Cache scaling is a non-issue: Even at 100M impressions/day x 16 bytes = 1.6 GB = tiny. Use Redis Cluster

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: for horizontal scale, with replicas + persistence (RDB/AOF) for failover, and the cache will comfortably

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: handle the load.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: 4) Ensuring Low-Latency Advertiser Queries

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Already largely solved by pre-aggregation in the pipeline: Whether using batch (Spark) or stream processing

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: (Flink), data is pre-aggregated before landing in the OLAP database. Advertisers query already-summarized

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: data instead of scanning raw click events, making typical queries fast out of the box.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Large time-window queries are the remaining bottleneck: Aggregating over days, weeks, months, or years at

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: query time can still be slow because the OLAP DB has to scan and roll up many minute-level rows. This is

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: where additional optimization is needed.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Pre-aggregate at multiple granularities via rollup tables: Run a nightly cron job that aggregates minute-level

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: data into daily, weekly, or monthly rollup tables. Advertisers query the coarser table for high-level views (e.g.,

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: yearly trends) and drill down into finer tables only when needed — trading storage space for dramatic query

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: speedups on the most common access patterns (a form of caching).

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: 1) Functional Requirements:

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Users can click on an ad and be redirected to the advertiser's website

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Advertisers can query ad click metrics over time with a minimum granularity of 1 minute

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: ---- out of scope-----

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Ad targeting

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Ad serving

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Cross device tracking

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Integration with offline marketing channels

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: 2) Non Functional Requirements (SPARCS):

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Scalability: support 10M ads at any given time, 10k ad clicks per sec at peak.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Low Latency: in terms of the query time

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Fault tolerant and accurate data collection. We should not lose any click data.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - As realtime as possible. Advertisers should be able to query data as soon as possible after

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: the click.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Idempotent click tracking. We should not count the same click multiple times.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: ---- Out of Scope --------

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Fraud or spam detection

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Demographic and geo profiling of users

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Conversion tracking

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: 3) System Interface

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: For data processing questions like this one, it helps to start by defining the system's

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: interface. This includes clearly outline what data the system receives and what it outputs,

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: establishing a clear boundary of the system's functionality. The inputs and outputs of this

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: system are very simple, but it's important to get these right!

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Input:Ad click data from user

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Output: Ad click metric for the advertisers to search for.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: 4) Data Flow

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: sequential series of steps we'll cover in order to get from the inputs to our system to the

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: outputs.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - User clicks on an ad on a website.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - The click is tracked and stored in the system.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - The user is redirected to the advertiser's website.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Advertisers query the system for aggregated click metrics.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Design Add Click Aggregator

text.font-family: Lilita One, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Design

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Potential Deep Dives

text.font-family: Lilita One, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: High Level Design

text.font-family: Lilita One, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Deep Dive

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: An Ad Click Aggregator is a system that collects and aggregates data on ad clicks. It is used by advertisers to track the performance of their ads and optimize their campaigns. For our

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: purposes, we will assume these are ads displayed on a website or app, like Facebook.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Key Concepts on the go

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: 1) When a user clicks on an ad which was placed by the Ad Placement Service, we will send a request to

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: our /click endpoint, which will track the click and then redirect the user to the advertiser's website. Add

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: placement service is like a black box for now.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: 2) Handling The redirect :

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Client Side:

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > When a user clicks on the ad, the browser will automatically redirect them to the target URL. It's

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: simple, straightforward, and requires no additional server side logic. We would then, in parallel, POST to

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: our /click endpoint to track the click.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > downside with this approach is that users could go to an advertiser's website without us knowing

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: about it. This could lead to discrepancies in our click data

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Servier Side:

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > user click on the ad, which will then send a request to our server. Our server can then track the click

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: and respond with a redirect to the advertiser's website via a 302 (redirect) status code.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > challenge is added load and complexity

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: 3) Querying Ad Click metrics

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Bad Solution:

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > store and qry from same database.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > store in db based on userid and ad id. then query based on the ad id using a group by.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > this solution sucks. The database will quickly become a bottleneck as we scale up to 10k clicks per

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: second. The GROUP BY query will be slow and inefficient, and we won't be able to provide low latency

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: queries to advertisers

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Good Solution:

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > use a separate analytics database with pre-aggregated data for low-latency queries.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > Raw click -> Event DB -> Batch processing -> Analytics DB.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > Event Db: Optimized for very high write throughput. Uses LSM tree storage structure. Writes first

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: go to an append-only commit log (durability). Then to an in-memory sorted memtable. Memtables are

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: periodically flushed to disk as SSTables. SSTables are good for row reads but poor for range queries and

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: aggregations. This is why batch pre-aggregation is needed.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > Batch Processing(Apache Spark): Distributed computing engine using the MapReduce paradigm. Reads

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: raw events in parallel chunks. Aggregates events by ad ID and minute timestamp. Writes aggregated

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: results into the analytics DB.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > BOE Calculations: 10K clicks/sec with 5-minute batches = 3M events per batch. ~100 bytes per

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: event = ~300 MB per batch. Small enough for a single machine, but Spark gives scalability. Spark also

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: offers a clean MapReduce model that's easy to explain in interviews.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > Analytical Db: Good choices: Redshift, Snowflake, BigQuery. Uses columnar storage for fast

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: aggregation queries. Excellent for COUNT, SUM, AVG over millions of rows. Optimized for read-heavy

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: analytical workloads.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > challenge: Batch processing causes stale data and cascades under load: Advertisers always see data

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: that is a few minutes old, and during traffic spikes the event store faces write pressure while batch jobs

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: take longer than their interval — leading to increasingly delayed insights exactly when real-time visibility

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: matters most (e.g., big ad launches).

g.text: - Great Solution:

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > Stream-based architecture replaces batch jobs: Click events flow directly into a stream (Kafka or

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Kinesis), where a stream processor (Flink or Spark Streaming) aggregates them in real-time and writes

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: results to the OLAP database for near real-time advertiser queries.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > Why Flink over plain Kafka consumers: Flink provides windowed aggregations with event-time

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: semantics (handles out-of-order events correctly), watermarks (knows when to safely close a window),

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: exactly-once processing guarantees, and built-in fault tolerance with state recovery — all of which are

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: painful and error-prone to build manually.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > Event time vs processing time: Flink uses event time (when the click actually happened) instead of

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: processing time (when Flink received it), ensuring accurate minute-bucket aggregations even when events

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: arrive late or out of order.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > Much finer latency control than batch: Stream aggregation windows can be shrunk to a few seconds,

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: which is impractical for Spark batch jobs due to overhead. Even better, Flink can aggregate on minute

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: boundaries but flush partial results every few seconds — giving low latency while still producing clean,

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: complete minute-level aggregates.
